discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of primordial density perturbations
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of accelerated expansion solves the horizon, flatness and monopole problems. Linde developed new and chaotic inflation, which made the idea into a workable, predictive framework. Mukhanov (with Chibisov) showed that quantum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure, and predicted a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted spectrum of adiabatic, Gaussian perturbations. Over the next four decades, precision observations confirmed these predictions one by one: COBE, WMAP, Planck, ACT and SPT measured acoustic peaks consistent with adiabatic superhorizon perturbations, found a spatially flat universe, found Gaussianity, and measured a spectral index n_s of about 0.965, clearly below one. Few theoretical ideas about the first instants of the universe have been so decisively tested. Inflation turned speculation about the Big Bang's initial conditions into quantitative, empirical science, and its gravitational-wave prediction continues to drive the CMB B-mode experimental programme.
